quests.hint: PUTTING CASH ASIDE INSTEAD OF USING IT RIGHT AWAY
quests.explanation: SAVE MONEY means to keep it for later rather than spending it. SAVE pairs with MONEY the way it does with time or energy — something you keep for future use.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: build MONEY like a wall over years
collect MONEY like stamps only
quests.contextSentence: They decided to save some ___ every month toward a house deposit.

quests.hint: USING YOUR CASH TO BUY THE THINGS YOU WANT OR NEED
quests.explanation: SPEND MONEY means to use it to pay for something. SPEND is the direct opposite of SAVE in this context — one keeps money, the other uses it up.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this contrasting habit.
wrongCollocations: waste MONEY as the only meaning of spend
burn MONEY literally in a fire
quests.contextSentence: He tends to spend too much ___ on gadgets he never really uses.

quests.hint: MAKING THE FINAL PAYMENT SO YOU NO LONGER OWE ANYTHING
quests.explanation: PAY OFF A LOAN means to finish repaying it completely. PAY OFF implies reaching zero balance, unlike simply PAY, which can mean just making one payment toward it.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this financial milestone.
wrongCollocations: finish a LOAN like a race only symbolically
close a LOAN like a door
quests.contextSentence: It took them nearly ten years to pay off their student ___.

quests.hint: SENDING YOUR RESUME AND COVER LETTER TO REQUEST A POSITION
quests.explanation: APPLY FOR A JOB means to formally request consideration for a position, usually by submitting an application. APPLY FOR is followed by the position or opportunity you want.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: request a JOB like a favor casually
beg a JOB from a manager directly
quests.contextSentence: After months of searching, she finally applied for a ___ at the design studio.

quests.hint: FORMALLY TELLING YOUR EMPLOYER, IN WRITING, THAT YOU'RE LEAVING THE JOB
quests.explanation: HAND IN YOUR RESIGNATION means to formally submit your notice that you're quitting. HAND IN is used for official documents you formally submit, such as a resignation letter or a report.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this career decision.
wrongCollocations: give up your RESIGNATION as a possession
throw your RESIGNATION away
quests.contextSentence: After accepting the new offer, he handed in his ___ the very next day.

quests.hint: MOVING UP TO A HIGHER POSITION AT WORK, USUALLY WITH MORE PAY
quests.explanation: GET A PROMOTION means to be moved up to a higher position. GET pairs with PROMOTION the way it does with many achievements you receive rather than actively build yourself.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this career milestone.
wrongCollocations: win a PROMOTION like a prize randomly
earn a PROMOTION only through luck
quests.contextSentence: After three strong years at the company, she finally got a well-deserved ___.

quests.hint: PERFORMING AS WELL AS YOUR BOSS OR CLIENT HOPED YOU WOULD
quests.explanation: MEET EXPECTATIONS means to perform at the level others hoped for. MEET is used broadly for reaching a required standard — meet expectations, meet a target, meet a requirement.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: reach EXPECTATIONS physically like a shelf
touch EXPECTATIONS with your hand
quests.contextSentence: The new intern quickly proved he could meet the team's ___.

quests.hint: TELLING SOMEONE HOW WELL OR POORLY THEY DID SOMETHING, SO THEY CAN IMPROVE
quests.explanation: GIVE FEEDBACK means to share your evaluation of someone's work. GIVE pairs with FEEDBACK the way it does with advice or an opinion — something you offer to another person.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this workplace habit.
wrongCollocations: make FEEDBACK appear out of nowhere
do FEEDBACK to a colleague physically
quests.contextSentence: Good managers give honest ___ regularly, not just once a year.

quests.hint: BEING ON THE OTHER SIDE — LISTENING TO SOMEONE'S EVALUATION OF YOUR WORK
quests.explanation: RECEIVE FEEDBACK means to be given someone's evaluation of your work. RECEIVE is the opposite side of GIVE — one person offers it, the other takes it in.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this contrasting experience.
wrongCollocations: catch FEEDBACK like a ball thrown at you
accept FEEDBACK only in writing
quests.contextSentence: It isn't always easy to receive ___ about your own work without feeling defensive.

quests.hint: TRANSFERRING SOMETHING FROM THE INTERNET ONTO YOUR OWN DEVICE
quests.explanation: DOWNLOAD A FILE means to transfer it from the internet onto your device. DOWNLOAD is the opposite of UPLOAD, which sends a file from your device to the internet.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: upload a FILE onto your own computer
print a FILE directly from the cloud
quests.contextSentence: It took almost ten minutes to download the ___ because the connection was slow.

quests.hint: CHANGING YOUR LOGIN CODE BECAUSE YOU FORGOT THE OLD ONE
quests.explanation: RESET YOUR PASSWORD means to create a new one, usually after forgetting the old one. RESET is used for restoring settings or credentials to a fresh, working state.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this login problem.
wrongCollocations: renew your PASSWORD like a subscription
recharge your PASSWORD like a battery
quests.contextSentence: After three failed attempts, the website asked her to reset her ___.

quests.hint: LINKING YOUR DEVICE TO A WIRELESS INTERNET NETWORK
quests.explanation: CONNECT TO WI-FI means to link your device to a wireless network. CONNECT TO is followed by whatever network or device you're linking to, such as Wi-Fi, a printer, or Bluetooth speakers.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this everyday tech action.
wrongCollocations: plug into WI-FI with a cable physically
attach WI-FI to your laptop with tape
quests.contextSentence: The cafe's password wasn't working, so we couldn't connect to the ___.

quests.hint: GETTING COMPLETELY BETTER, WITH NO LASTING EFFECTS FROM THE ILLNESS
quests.explanation: MAKE A FULL RECOVERY means to get entirely better after being sick or injured. MAKE pairs with RECOVERY in this fixed medical expression, describing a return to complete health.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: do a RECOVERY like a chore
build a RECOVERY brick by brick
quests.contextSentence: Doctors say he's expected to make a full ___ within a few weeks.

quests.hint: LIVING WITH A CONDITION THAT CAUSES YOU DISCOMFORT ON A REGULAR BASIS
quests.explanation: SUFFER FROM AN ALLERGY means to regularly experience its symptoms. SUFFER FROM is followed by an ongoing condition, such as an allergy, a headache, or insomnia.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this health condition.
wrongCollocations: carry an ALLERGY around like luggage
hold an ALLERGY like an object
quests.contextSentence: Every spring, he suffers from a bad ___ to pollen.

quests.hint: HAVING A SHOT AT THE CLINIC THAT PROTECTS YOU AGAINST A DISEASE
quests.explanation: GET VACCINATED means to receive a vaccine shot. GET combines with VACCINATED the way it does with other outcomes you receive from a medical visit, like get examined or get treated.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this preventive health step.
wrongCollocations: make VACCINATED yourself at home
do VACCINATED without a doctor
quests.contextSentence: Before traveling abroad, it's a good idea to get ___ against common local illnesses.

quests.hint: OFFICIALLY REQUESTING A PRODUCT FROM A STORE OR WEBSITE
quests.explanation: PLACE AN ORDER means to formally request a product, usually online. PLACE is used in this fixed business expression, unlike everyday speech where people might simply say 'order something.'
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: put an ORDER somewhere physically like a shelf
set an ORDER like a table
quests.contextSentence: She placed an ___ for the new shoes as soon as they came back in stock.

quests.hint: FOLLOWING A DELIVERY'S PROGRESS ONLINE TO SEE WHERE IT IS
quests.explanation: TRACK A PACKAGE means to monitor its delivery progress online. TRACK is used whenever you follow the movement or progress of something, such as a package, a flight, or your spending.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this delivery habit.
wrongCollocations: follow a PACKAGE around on foot personally
chase a PACKAGE down the street
quests.contextSentence: You can track your ___ using the number in the confirmation email.

quests.hint: WRITING YOUR OPINION OF A PRODUCT ONLINE AFTER USING IT
quests.explanation: LEAVE A REVIEW means to write your opinion of something online, typically after a purchase. LEAVE is used here the way it is with feedback or a comment — something you post for others to see.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this online habit.
wrongCollocations: do a REVIEW physically with a pen only
make a REVIEW appear automatically
quests.contextSentence: After the trip, she left a glowing ___ for the small hotel.

quests.hint: REGISTERING YOUR ARRIVAL AT THE FRONT DESK AND GETTING YOUR ROOM KEY
quests.explanation: CHECK IN AT A HOTEL means to register your arrival and collect your room key. CHECK IN is also used at airports, but the process and location differ.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: enter a HOTEL like a race checkpoint
sign a HOTEL like a contract
quests.contextSentence: We arrived late, but the ___ let us check in without any trouble.

quests.hint: ARRIVING TOO LATE TO CATCH THE NEXT FLIGHT IN A MULTI-STOP JOURNEY
quests.explanation: MISS A CONNECTION means to arrive too late to catch a following flight or train. MISS pairs with anything time-sensitive you fail to catch, such as a connection, a bus, or a deadline.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this travel mishap.
wrongCollocations: lose a CONNECTION like an object dropped
drop a CONNECTION accidentally
quests.contextSentence: The first flight was delayed, so they nearly missed their ___ in Frankfurt.

quests.hint: SWAPPING ONE COUNTRY'S MONEY FOR ANOTHER BEFORE A TRIP ABROAD
quests.explanation: EXCHANGE CURRENCY means to convert money from one country into another. EXCHANGE is used specifically for swapping one form of money, or one item, for an equivalent.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this pre-trip task.
wrongCollocations: trade CURRENCY like baseball cards casually
swap CURRENCY like clothes at a party
quests.contextSentence: Before flying to Japan, they stopped at the airport to exchange some ___.

quests.hint: SAYING SOMETHING TO EASE THE AWKWARDNESS WHEN MEETING SOMEONE NEW
quests.explanation: BREAK THE ICE means to say or do something to ease initial awkwardness in a new social situation. BREAK THE ICE is a fixed idiom, always used with THE ICE, never another word.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: melt the ICE using humor literally
crack the ICE with a joke physically
quests.contextSentence: He told a silly joke to break the ___ at the start of the meeting.

quests.hint: CHATTING CASUALLY WITH SOMEONE ABOUT UNIMPORTANT, EVERYDAY TOPICS
quests.explanation: MAKE CONVERSATION means to talk casually, often with someone you don't know well. MAKE pairs with CONVERSATION when you're the one initiating or sustaining the talk, unlike INTERRUPT, which disrupts it.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this social skill.
wrongCollocations: build CONVERSATION brick by brick slowly
cook CONVERSATION like a meal
quests.contextSentence: At the wedding, she found it easy to make ___ with total strangers.

quests.hint: EACH PERSON WAITING PATIENTLY FOR THEIR CHANCE TO SPEAK OR ACT
quests.explanation: TAKE TURNS means to do something one after another, rather than all at once. TAKE pairs with TURNS in this fixed phrase, describing fair, orderly sharing of a chance to act.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this fairness rule.
wrongCollocations: share TURNS by cutting them physically in half
split TURNS like a cake
quests.contextSentence: The children were told to take ___ on the swing so everyone got a chance.

quests.hint: GRADUALLY EARNING SOMEONE'S CONFIDENCE THROUGH HONESTY OVER TIME
quests.explanation: BUILD TRUST means to gradually earn someone's confidence through consistent, honest behavior. BUILD pairs with TRUST the way it does with a relationship — something strengthened slowly over time.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make TRUST appear overnight instantly
buy TRUST with money directly
quests.contextSentence: It takes consistent honesty to build real ___ with your team.

quests.hint: HAVING SOMEONE STOP BELIEVING IN YOU AFTER YOU'VE LET THEM DOWN
quests.explanation: LOSE TRUST means someone stops believing in you, usually after being let down. LOSE is the opposite of BUILD here — one strengthens confidence, the other destroys it.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this damaging outcome.
wrongCollocations: drop TRUST like an object accidentally
spill TRUST like a drink
quests.contextSentence: After being caught lying twice, he quickly lost his colleagues' ___.

quests.hint: SAYING SORRY FOR SOMETHING SPECIFIC YOU DID WRONG
quests.explanation: APOLOGIZE FOR A MISTAKE means to say sorry for something specific you did wrong. APOLOGIZE FOR is followed by the exact thing you regret, unlike simply saying SORRY on its own.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this formal apology.
wrongCollocations: excuse a MISTAKE like forgiving a debt
forgive a MISTAKE toward yourself only
quests.contextSentence: The company sent an email to apologize for the ___ in last month's billing.

quests.hint: BRINGING UP SOMETHING THAT'S WORRYING YOU SO OTHERS ARE AWARE OF IT
quests.explanation: RAISE A CONCERN means to formally mention something that's worrying you. RAISE is used for bringing up an issue, a question, or a concern so others can address it.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: lift a CONCERN physically off the ground
carry a CONCERN in your arms
quests.contextSentence: During the meeting, she raised a ___ about the tight delivery schedule.

quests.hint: MOVING STEADILY CLOSER TO A GOAL, EVEN IF SLOWLY
quests.explanation: MAKE PROGRESS means to move steadily toward completing or achieving something. MAKE pairs with PROGRESS the way it does with an effort or an improvement — something built up gradually.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this sense of achievement.
wrongCollocations: do PROGRESS overnight suddenly
build PROGRESS like a wall brick by brick only literally
quests.contextSentence: After weeks of practice, he finally started to make real ___ with the language.

quests.hint: SUCCEEDING IN REACHING SOMETHING YOU SET OUT TO DO
quests.explanation: ACHIEVE A GOAL means to succeed in reaching something you aimed for. ACHIEVE is used for outcomes reached through effort, such as a goal, a target, or a dream.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this sense of success.
wrongCollocations: win a GOAL like a prize randomly
catch a GOAL like a ball thrown
quests.contextSentence: With hard work and patience, she finally achieved her ___ of running a marathon.
